flags: Cache confirms Visit NH promotes a byway, but supplies neither a formal designation record nor a designation date. No state-designation assertion is made.

Visit NH describes a 98-mile trip; material maps 70.9 miles. Omitted distance and followed ascending strip-map order from the Pittsburg/Stewartstown side toward Gorham, reversing the tourism itinerary.
Dixville Notch sources conflict about the current polling room and The Balsams operations. Dropped the current ballroom claim and did not promise hotel access.

The current unqualified first-reporting claim is replaced by the documented 1964 event; the cache warns that claims of always voting first are erroneous. Population of four is dated 2020, not treated as current.
Errol’s road petition chronology says 1789 petition and 1781 approval; omitted it. Road history uses the Coos Trail instead.

Pontook is kept short because its dedicated page is thin; no paddling difficulty superlative is retained from the interleaved PDF extraction. No cached official present-day park operations source was supplied.
Cache documents older trade corridors but no creation date or campaign for the modern Moose Path Trail. Intro keeps those histories separate.
